summary: Persimmon, parsley and olive salad: flat-leaf parsley leaves used as the "lettuce", tossed with diced Fuyu persimmon and pitted black olives, olive oil, sherry vinegar, salt and pepper; a palate-cleansing side for 4 that takes under a minute to assemble.
glance: 10 minutes; final assembly under a minute
2 Fuyu (not Hachiya), peeled if needed, medium dice
1 bunch flat-leaf, leaves and very thin stems
faq: Which persimmons should I use?

Only Fuyu persimmons: the squat ones eaten crisp. Hachiyas, which are more oblong, are inedibly astringent until they are as soft as pudding. Fuyu flavor is moderately sweet and flowery with a slight tang and muskiness, somewhat similar to mango.
Do I need to peel the persimmon?
Generally yes, unless the skin is surprisingly tender. The author recommends a Zyliss soft skin peeler for peeling fruit, including tomatoes.
Why use parsley as the lettuce?
It might seem strange, but it isn't something you eat a huge plate of; it is more an accompaniment to cleanse the palate. Use flat-leaf Italian parsley; curly wouldn't be good here.
Can I make it ahead?
Everything can be prepared in advance, but don't toss until you're ready to serve because it will all wilt. Final assembly takes less than a minute.
What can I add?
Fresh mint or basil, and thinly sliced red onion or scallion. The author normally makes the salad with blood oranges later in the winter.

summary: Sesame corn muffins based on a Joy of Cooking recipe: cornmeal, flour and 1/2 cup of sesame seeds with buttermilk (or buttermilk powder, or yogurt), mixed just to moisten, topped with more seeds and baked at 425°F for 20-25 minutes (15 on convection); makes 12.
glance: 2/3 cup buttermilk, or 1/2 cup water plus 2 1/2 tablespoons powder, or 2/3 cup yogurt
faq: Why add sesame to corn muffins?
Sesame and corn go great together, emphasizing the earthy flavors in each. The seeds go in the batter and more on top.
Can I use buttermilk powder?

Yes. The author used Saco buttermilk powder (2 1/2 tablespoons powder to 2/3 cup water), but that made the batter a bit thin, so the recipe uses less water. Add the powder to the dry ingredients and the water to the wet ones.
Which sesame seeds should I use?

Hulled or unhulled, toasted or raw all work; the author used hulled, untoasted ones. If using untoasted ones, give the ones in the batter a quick toast, but don't pretoast the topping seeds or they might burn.
How do I keep the muffins tender?
Mix just well enough to moisten; lumps are fine. Do not overbeat or they will become tough.
How do I know they're done?
A toothpick comes out clean, in about 20-25 minutes in a regular oven or 15 on convection.

summary: Morel "hot chocolate" soup, a dipping soup for savory churros: cream steeped with dried morels (10 minutes simmering, 30 resting), blended with unsweetened cocoa, half-and-half and salt, strained and frothed; serves 4 as a tiny appetizer, about 1/2 cup per person.
glance: 4 as a tiny appetizer (about 1/2 cup each)
10 minutes on the lowest heat, then rest 30 minutes
1.5 cups cream, 0.6 ounce dried morels, 2 teaspoons cocoa, 1/2 cup half & half
rolled in smoked paprika, cinnamon and salt
faq: What are churros?

Popular throughout Spain and much of Latin America, often as a breakfast treat or street food, served with thick hot chocolate. They can be thick or thin, straight or knotted, made from a potato or wheat flour dough, but are always extruded and fried like a doughnut.
How is churro dough made?
Similar in conception to a choux paste: make a hot mixture of flour, butter and water, then beat in eggs. The author used a recipe from Michelle Bernstein.
How do the churros become savory?
Roll them in smoked paprika (pimenton dulce), cinnamon and salt instead of cinnamon and sugar.
Why put chocolate in a mushroom soup?
As in a mole, chocolate used without sugar gives a subtle, earthy, slightly bitter note that marries easily with the morels. Use high-quality cocoa powder, not Hershey's.
How rich is it?
Rich, so plan on only about 1/2 cup per person. It would also make a fine first course without the churros; for service the author plans to froth it with a handheld blender and serve in a demitasse.

summary: Spanish lentils and mushrooms: French green lentils simmered with onion and garlic and seasoned with smoked paprika and sherry vinegar, topped with thick-cut crimini mushrooms browned in a very hot pan and a cherry tomato and basil salad; vegan, serves 4-6 in about 40 minutes.
glance: 2 cups French green (or de Puy or black Beluga) with 4 cups water
1 pound crimini, quartered lengthwise, browned well
faq: Which lentils work?
French green lentils (lentils de Puy) or black Beluga lentils. Standard big green or brown lentils will turn to mush.
Why quarter the mushrooms and brown them?
Mushrooms cut thickly and browned are a completely different experience from thinly sliced and sauteed: the surface gets seared and the interior stays chewy rather than cooking all the water out.
How should the lentils taste?
Seasoned with salt, sherry vinegar and smoked paprika, with just an edge of vinegary sourness that isn't overpowering.
What is the tomato salad for?
With earthy, brown plates the author loves to finish with something bright and fresh: cherry tomatoes and basil tossed with a little olive oil, sherry vinegar and salt.
How do I serve it?
With a good baguette it makes a nice light, healthy meal, or a smaller portion can be the first course of something more elaborate.

summary: Farro, chanterelles and King apples as a hot entree: farro with toasted caraway, sauteed apples, chanterelles flamed with Calvados, and an apple "balsamic" vinegar sauce emulsified with butter, all built in one pan; serves 4.
glance: 2 cups whole or semi-pearled, about 45 minutes (less if semi-pearled)
1/3 cup Acetoria apple vinegar reduced a few seconds, whisked with 8 tablespoons butter in pats
4 generous handfuls of chanterelles, sauteed then finished with 1/4 cup Calvados
faq: Why pair farro with chanterelles and apples?

Chanterelles speak of fall and have no substitute once sauteed; farro's nuttiness complements the fruit and mushrooms. Toasted caraway seeds in the farro add another autumnal flavor. The author also made a cold salad version.
How do I build the sauce?

Saute the apples and then the chanterelles in the same pan without cleaning it, remove the mushrooms, reduce the apple vinegar a few seconds (it's already quite thick), and whisk in the butter pats one at a time to emulsify, like a beurre blanc but not blanc.
Is flaming the Calvados safe?
There is a chance the alcohol will flame up, so be prepared and careful. Skip this step and omit the Calvados if you don't feel comfortable with the risk.
What if I can't find apple balsamic?

Use Acetoria apple vinegar, not regular cider vinegar. The author's guess for a substitute is to reduce good apple juice with cider vinegar, sugar and maybe apple butter, though it wouldn't be the same.
How do I plate it?

Place a ring mold in the center of a plate, fill with 1 cup of farro, top with chanterelles, spread 1/4 of the sauce on the plate, sprinkle the sauteed apples around, and finish with chives and sea salt.

summary: A farmers' market feast bowl: smoked paprika quinoa cakes fried 2-3 minutes per side, spicy roasted corn relish, pan-fried zucchini, beefsteak tomato and cucumber salad, and a simple parsley chimichurri to tie them together; serves 4.
glance: 2 cups leftover quinoa, 2 eggs, 1/4 cup per cake, 1/4 inch thick, 2-3 minutes per side
4 small, 1/4-inch slabs, pan-fried in a single layer on high heat
each can be a side in a different meal
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you use an egg-replacer in the cakes
faq: How do I make quinoa cakes hold together?

Combine the cooked, cooled quinoa with salt, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano and 2 eggs: you should have a dough that forms a wet ball. If it's still dry and fluffy, add another egg. Form 1/4-cup pancakes about 1/4 inch thick.
How do I cook the quinoa cakes?

Use your largest skillet or a flat griddle pan at medium-high heat with a thin layer of oil, cook until golden brown on one side, about 2-3 minutes, then flip and finish the other side. Season with salt and pepper.
How should zucchini be cooked?

Pan-fried in a single layer over a high flame without crowding. The author says almost no one realizes how good it is: with lots of surface area and a hot flame it develops a nutty, caramelized flavor that is addictive. Pat the slabs dry and cook until lots of brown spots form on each side.
How do I make the chimichurri?

Process olive oil, garlic, parsley, salt, pepper and sherry vinegar or lemon juice in a mini food processor to a thin sauce, like a pesto without the nuts or cheese. Let it rest so the flavor develops.
Can I use components separately?
Yes. Any one could be a good side dish in a different meal, so mix and match.

summary: Bangla-flavored fried zucchini, adapted from Alford and Duguid's Mangoes & Curry Leaves (with a review): zucchini slabs fried 3-5 minutes in a wok with a little oil, turmeric, black mustard seeds, cayenne and sugar; vegan, serves 4.
glance: 3-5 minutes, until tender but not mush
turmeric, black mustard seeds, cayenne, sugar, fried about 10 seconds first
Mangoes & Curry Leaves: Culinary Travels Through the Great Subcontinent
faq: What is Mangoes & Curry Leaves about?
A cookbook by Jeffrey Alford and Naomi Duguid devoted to the foods of Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, with travel stories as well as recipes.
What is the authors' approach?

The recipes are what people really eat: simple and unfussy but full of flavor and character. They don't obsess about false authenticity but don't dumb down the food, and offer substitutions when an ingredient is hard to find.
What does zucchini replace in this recipe?
The original uses a gourd called potol, which is hard to find, so the authors recommend zucchini with the same cooking technique.
Can I use more oil?

The original uses lots of oil, which ends up highly flavored and can be reused as the base of another stir-fry. The author used much less for a healthy weeknight supper; for the full version, use 2 tablespoons each of mustard oil and vegetable oil and reduce the mustard seeds to 1/4 teaspoon.
What do I serve with it?
The author ate it with tamarind-flavored rice and jarred lime pickle; add a dal, flatbread and raita and/or chutneys for a real feast.

summary: A 6-inch Momofuku Milk Bar-style strawberries and cream birthday cake (serves 8): layers cut with a cake ring from a sheet cake, filled with strawberries macerated 30 minutes, moistened with their juice and frosted with cream cheese-stabilized whipped cream; the cake itself is from Christina Tosi's book.
glance: 1 pound sliced 1/4 inch, macerated with 1/2 cup sugar about 30 minutes
the juice from macerating the strawberries
8 ounces cream cheese, 1 cup powdered sugar, 1 1/2 cups heavy cream
quarter sheet pan, 6-inch cake ring, acetate collars
faq: What is the Momofuku Milk Bar cake method?

Christina Tosi bakes a sheet cake, then uses a cake ring to cut out two layers. The bottom layer is made by pressing all the scraps into the ring. Acetate collars keep the outside smooth so the filling shows. The cake recipe (Birthday Cake, page 105) and assembly are in her cookbook, which the author doesn't reproduce.
What tools do I need?
The Momofuku Milk Bar cookbook, a quarter sheet pan (the author avoids non-stick), a 6-inch cake ring (he likes Fat Daddio's) and acetate collars.
What are the filling, soak and frosting?

The author's own: macerated strawberries are the filling, the juice from macerating them is the soak for moistening the layers, and the frosting is whipped cream stabilized with full-fat cream cheese so it doesn't collapse under the weight of the cake.
How do I macerate the strawberries?

Cut off the stems, slice the berries 1/4 inch parallel to the base, toss with 1/2 cup sugar and leave at room temperature, tossing occasionally, until softened and juicy, about 30 minutes. Save the juice.
How do I make the frosting?

Beat 8 ounces of cream cheese, salt, 1 cup of powdered sugar and 1 tablespoon of vanilla until fluffy, about 1 minute, drizzle in 1 1/2 cups heavy cream with the mixer running, and beat to stiff peaks. Refrigerate until frosting.
Did the author add a crunchy component?
No; unlike the Momofuku style, the strawberries didn't seem to want one.

summary: Chirashi ("scattered") sushi bowls: seasoned sushi rice topped with seared eggplant, shiitake and beech mushrooms, browned tofu, shaved cucumber, avocado, kaiware, shiso, pickled ginger, wasabi and umeboshi; vegan, serves 4 in 45 minutes and easy to simplify.
glance: 2 cups Japanese rice with 6 tablespoons rice vinegar, 3 tablespoons sugar and 4 teaspoons salt
faq: What is chirashi sushi?
"Scattered" sushi, presented in a bowl instead of rolled up in nori sheets, so it is a lot simpler to make.
Do I need all the toppings?

No. This is a fairly elaborate version; you could make it with nothing but avocado and fried tofu and it would still be delicious. The author gets the rice cooking, then makes as many toppings as he has time for.
How do I season sushi rice?

Cook the rice, turn it out into a large shallow wooden bowl, sprinkle on the whisked vinegar, sugar and salt, and cut and fold with a paddle while fanning with the other hand, about 5 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is near room temperature. Don't stir or it will become mushy.
What other toppings can I use?
Others that fit the Japanese palette: pickled daikon, sweet omelet (tamago), tempura green beans or asparagus.
How do I prepare the cucumber?
Peel it, then shave it with the peeler into long thin sheets avoiding the seeds, and toss with rice wine vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Why make the wasabi visible?
So it isn't eaten accidentally when you arrange the toppings around the rice.

summary: Onion pakora: sliced onion tossed in a chickpea flour batter spiced with cumin, turmeric and cayenne (rested 15 minutes) and deep-fried at 360°F in 2-tablespoon portions for about 3 minutes until deep golden, served with tamarind or mint chutney; serves 3-4.
glance: 1 cup chickpea flour (besan) and 2/3 cup water, between pancake and crepe batter, rest 15 minutes
360°F, oil at least 3 inches deep, about 3 minutes
faq: What is pakora?

A classic Indian snack or appetizer made by coating just about any vegetable (or sometimes fruit) in a chickpea flour batter and deep frying. The pieces can be whole slices or smaller bits spooned together, and the batter thick or thin, crispy or puffy.
What is chickpea flour?

Called besan (pronounced bay-san) at an Indian grocery. It was once hard to find, but it is now widely available because of gluten-free baking. The author finds it unpleasant in most gluten-free baking, but perfect for pakora and many Indian savories, as well as socca. Bob's Red Mill makes a good one.
How thick should the batter be?
Definitely pourable but not too thin, somewhere between pancake batter and crepe batter. If too thick, whisk in a little more water; if too thin, a little more chickpea flour.
How do I cut the onion?

Halve it lengthwise and peel, cut each half in half again in the perpendicular direction, then slice each quarter into 1/4-inch slices (slightly thinner than 1/3 inch), separate and toss in the batter.
How do I fry them?

Heat oil at least 3 inches deep to 360°F, spoon in about 2 tablespoons of battered onion at a time, well separated, moving them with a spatula so they don't stick, and fry turning occasionally until deep golden brown, about 3 minutes.
What do I serve with pakora?
Something for dipping, most often tamarind chutney, which you can make or buy at an Indian grocery, or mint chutney.
